In summary, our research is concerned with
the role and impact of social and environmental reporting and accountability in society.
the social and environmental impacts of the activities of business organisations.
how the social and environmental accountability of business is being constructed in practice and the implications of this for society and the environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
social accounting research is still in its infancy and has a long way to go before it can claim to be a mature and established field of study.
the current state of social accounting research is not as bad as it is being made out to be.
there is no evidence to suggest that the current SEAR community is ‘homogeneous, faddish and herding’.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown how the field of social and environmental accountability research is not as homogenous as some would have it and that it is not necessarily the case that SEAR is faddish, herded and has lost its social significance.
we have been able to demonstrate the importance of the social and the environmental dimensions of the business enterprise.
we have shown that the social and environmental accounting literature is not homogeneous, that it is not faddish and that it is not herding at the expense of social significance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the field of social and environmental research has been too focused on the ‘how’ and the ‘why’ of social and environmental reporting, and not enough on the ‘what’ of the social and environmental issues being reported on.
we should all be asking ourselves whether we are contributing to social change.
